intro: Peterborough is a cathedral city on the River Nene in Cambridgeshire. On its western edge, beside Orton Hall in Orton Longueville, a broad path runs between two long lines of giant sequoias, the red-barked American giants that British estates planted in rows from the 1850s. A reader walked the avenue and sent us its biggest trunk, which they measured at almost six metres round.
meta_description: A giant sequoia in the avenue beside Orton Hall, Peterborough: a reader's tree, almost six metres round, and how to find it.

trees.story:
"A whole avenue of trees," is how the reader who sent us this sequoia described the place they found it, beside Orton Hall on the western edge of Peterborough.

Their photographs show what they mean. A broad earth path runs straight through the woods, and on either side of it stands a line of giant sequoias, their soft red trunks rising bare for a long way before the blue-green foliage begins. Ivy has climbed the nearest ones and browned in patches against the bark. This tree is the big trunk in the foreground on the left, thicker than any of its neighbours, and beyond it the line keeps going until the path disappears among the trunks.

Giant sequoias reached Britain in the 1850s, and estates up and down the country planted them in rows like this one as soon as they could, so a Victorian avenue of them is a familiar sight. A walk between two lines of them is not.

The reader measured this one at 589 centimetres round and puts it at about 150 years old. Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen. If you know when the avenue was planted, or who planted it, tell us here.

Walk the length of the path and look up as you pass each spire.
trees.how_to_recognise: On a broad earth path lined on both sides with tall red-barked sequoias: the thick, ivy-clad trunk wider than any of its neighbours in the line.
trees.access: The reader photographed it from the broad path through the avenue beside Orton Hall. We have not confirmed who owns the ground or when the path is open; check before you go.
